review_evidence: README describes Batteries as the extended “batteries included” Lean library for both computer-science and mathematics applications.
The hydrated snapshot has 260 Lean files and direct scan found roughly 1,389 theorem declarations plus hundreds of checked examples across production modules.

For example Batteries/Classes/Order.lean develops Lawful comparison/order interfaces and transitivity/equivalence theorems, showing that the source contains reusable formal specifications and proofs rather than only runtime utilities.
summary: Retain Batteries as a large theorem-bearing foundational library of data structures, algebraic/order interfaces, algorithms, tactics, and proved laws.

summary: Inspected all 183 changed/added files in the leanprover-community__batteries repository. The files comprise: (1) core mathematical libraries (Data/, Control/, Classes/, Logic.lean, Recycling/RBTree/, Recycling/MonadSatisfying/) with theorems, lemmas, typeclass instances, and data structure definitions; (2) meta-programming infrastructure (CodeAction/, Tactic/, Linter/, Lean/Meta/, Util/ProofWanted.lean) containing formal tactic, code-action, and linter implementations with real def/theorem/instance/class declarations; (3) test fixtures (BatteriesTest/*.lean) with #guard and example declarations exercising library features; (4) six pure import aggregators (CodeAction.lean, Linter.lean, Tactic/Basic.lean, Lean/SatisfiesM.lean, Classes/SatisfiesM.lean, Recycling/MonadSatisfying/Lean.lean). The prior review (RRV-602c03909116-r2) classified categories (1)-(3) as genuine content. Per FILTER-007, pure import aggregators are navigation data for downranking (navigation-import-only), not hard exclusion. No CI/maintenance scripts other than the already-excluded scripts/check_imports.lean are present. Per FILTER-002/004/021/025, the high evidence bar for hard exclusion is unmet; default retain applies to all files.
